query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of molybdenum (Mo) to a high-entropy alloy (HEA) designed as a single-phase solid solution will preserve its toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading.
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure at 700°C and subsequent loading
generation.structural_mediator: Solid solution strengthening and grain refinement
generation.mechanism: Mo addition promotes solid solution strengthening, reduces grain size, and inhibits phase segregation, thereby preserving toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved toughness and resistance to thermal softening
generation.baseline: Same alloy without Mo addition, tested under identical conditions
generation.boundary: Thermal exposure temperature and duration, loading conditions
generation.uncertainty: Optimal Mo content, potential interactions with other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the toughness of HEAs with and without Mo addition after thermal exposure and loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the toughness of the Mo-containing HEA is not significantly higher than that of the Mo-free HEA, the hypothesis is falsified
